title: Water on Earth
seo_title: Grade 5 Water on Earth Worksheets: Salt Water, Fresh Water, Ice and Groundwater Graphs
standard_text: Describe and graph the amounts and percentages of water and fresh water in various reservoirs to provide evidence about the distribution of water on Earth.
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 science worksheets on water on Earth (NGSS 5-ESS2-2): 97% ocean and 3% fresh water, glaciers, groundwater, lakes and rivers, circle graphs and percent models. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: About 97% of Earth's water is salt water; only 3% is fresh.
key_sub: Most fresh water is frozen in ice (69%) or underground (30%). Only about 1% is in lakes, rivers and the air.
body_html:
How to think about it

Most of Earth is covered with water, but almost all of it is salt water in the ocean (about 97%). Only about 3% is fresh water.

Most fresh water is hard to use: about 69% is frozen in glaciers and ice caps and about 30% is groundwater under the ground. Only about 1% is in lakes, rivers, swamps and the air.

Example

If all of Earth's water were 1,000 liters, about how much would be fresh?

3% of 1,000

1,000 × 3 ÷ 100 = 30

Answer: about 30 liters

Example

Of 30 liters of fresh water, about how much is ice?

about 69%, a little more than two-thirds

about 21 liters

Answer: about 21 liters

Common mistakes

  • Thinking most water is fresh. Only about 3% is.
  • Thinking most fresh water is in lakes and rivers. Most is frozen.
  • Thinking groundwater is an underground lake. It fills tiny spaces in soil and rock.
  • Making a circle graph whose parts do not add up to 100%.

faq.q: How much of Earth's water is fresh?
faq.a: Only about 3%. About 97% is salt water in the ocean.

faq.q: Where is most of Earth's fresh water?
faq.a: About 69% is frozen in glaciers and ice caps, about 30% is groundwater, and only about 1% is in lakes, rivers, swamps and the air.
Water that soaks into the ground and fills the tiny spaces in soil and rock. People reach it with wells.
Only a tiny part of Earth's water is fresh and easy to reach, so it must be used carefully.

items.q: Why can't people drink ocean water?
c: It is too deep to reach.
It has no water in it.
items.e: Drinking salt water makes the body lose water. Fresh water is needed.

items.q: Is the water in an ocean salt water or fresh water?

Why is fresh water called a limited resource?

There is no fresh water left.
Fresh water can be made from nothing.
items.e: Most water is salty or frozen, so we must use fresh water carefully.
